title: Different behavior between debug and release exports for invalid `await` on runtime null
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.5.dev2 (af2c713971499953373380b9ae8673f64423bd59)
- Reproducible in 4.4.stable and 4.3.stable, likely earlier too

### System information

Fedora 41, not OS specific

### Issue description

We seem to have an inconsistency between debug and release export templates for the way `await object.some_signal` deals with errors when `object` turns out to be invalid/null at runtime.

See this example code from the MRP, which similates a runtime null target by removing self from the tree, and awaiting `get_tree().process_frame`:
```gdscript
extends Node

var _run_loop = 5
# Setting this to true triggers the bug in this example.
var _remove_from_tree = true

func do_stuff():
	print("Did stuff")

func _process(delta):
	if _remove_from_tree and get_parent():
		get_parent().remove_child(self)

	print("Start loop")

	while _run_loop > 0:
		await get_tree().process_frame
		do_stuff()
		_run_loop -= 1

	print("End loop")
```

In the editor or a debug template, this prints (line numbers from `4.4.stable`):
```
Start loop
ERROR: Parameter "data.tree" is null.
   at: get_tree (scene/main/node.h:485)
SCRIPT ERROR: Invalid access to property or key 'process_frame' on a base object of type 'null instance'.
          at: _process (res://node.gd:17)
```

But in a release template, this prints:
```
Start loop
ERROR: Parameter "data.tree" is null.
   at: get_tree (scene/main/node.h:485)
Did stuff
ERROR: Parameter "data.tree" is null.
   at: get_tree (scene/main/node.h:485)
Did stuff
ERROR: Parameter "data.tree" is null.
   at: get_tree (scene/main/node.h:485)
Did stuff
ERROR: Parameter "data.tree" is null.
   at: get_tree (scene/main/node.h:485)
Did stuff
ERROR: Parameter "data.tree" is null.
   at: get_tree (scene/main/node.h:485)
Did stuff
End loop
```
So here the loop keeps processing as if there was no `await` at all, while the debug version stops abruptly.

This is quite surprising to the user and makes for hard to debug errors when the code behaves so differently on release vs debug, which I would argue is a bug.

I'm not sure which behavior is best, but it should be consistent.

### Steps to reproduce

- Call `await` on an object/signal that's not valid at runtime

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[await_null.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19653288/await_null.zip)
